scope: Adversarial second-pass challenge of every earlier-phase finding for the platform-wide workflow audit. Read-only code walk; cites file paths + line numbers as evidence; no fixes applied here.
challenge_basis_note: Because only Phase 0 inventory + the pre-existing workflow_click_reduction_audit (2026-05-05) had landed, the challenge focuses on (a) the 6 workflows listed in workflow_click_reduction_audit, (b) workflows surfaced by Phase 0 inventory's per-app workflow_pages, (c) workflows the prompt's 12-question lens makes salient but earlier-phase artifacts entirely omit.

challenges_raised.prior_finding: workflow_click_reduction_audit.json: 'Teacher Workspace next-action strip opens attendance for the active class.' Implies low-click path is in place.
challenges_raised.my_finding: FALSE. templates/teacher/attendance.html lines 1-23 show no next_action_strip include, no primary 'Take attendance' button, and no workflow_next_action component. The ONLY top-of-page action is 'Export CSV' (lines 18, 20). Summary/History cards (lines 25-50) are read-only. The primary action (mark roll) lives below the fold inside a roster form, not at page-top. data-task="teacher_attendance" is present at line 7 but there is no surfaced 'next action' at all.

Hypothesis is not falsifiable in current code because the proposed primary action ('Take attendance') is not surfaced at all. The 1-2 click target cannot be reached from /portal/teacher/ as long as the dashboard does not link directly into the attendance entry form for the active class. Phase 0 inventory shows zero workflow_next_action.html include in any /templates/teacher/* template (verified via grep).

FALSE. The actual template uses data-task="teacher_marks_entry" (templates/teacher/marks_entry.html line 6 + line 50 + line 282). The audit's hook string does not match any template; downstream click-ingest analytics keyed on 'marks_entry' will silently produce zero events. This is a measurable telemetry gap, not just a naming nit.

challenges_raised.prior_finding: workflow_click_reduction_audit.json: 'Pending work card links directly to marks grid.'
challenges_raised.my_finding: PARTIAL. marks_entry.html has clearly labeled primary buttons (line 282 'Save All Marks', line 284 'submit_for_approval', line 50 'Load students'). The page itself is OK. But the claim that a 'Pending work card' (presumably on the teacher dashboard) links to it is unverifiable: no teacher dashboard template wires a 'pending work' card to marks_entry via data-task, and the phase 0 inventory does not list a teacher_dashboard.html under apps/portal workflow pages. The deep-link in is real; the dashboard entry-point is unverified.

challenges_raised.prior_finding: workflow_click_reduction_audit.json line 37: data_hooks include data-task="report_generation", primary_action 'Generate report'
challenges_raised.my_finding: PARTIAL. The string data-task="report_generation" exists ONLY in templates/analytics/decision_intelligence_dashboard.html (5 sites: lines 5, 25, 37, 49, 61) and in test files. The advertised 'Governed report builder' template templates/analytics/governed_report_builder.html uses data-task="governed_report_export" instead (lines 7, 54, 58, 65). So the report_generation telemetry name fragments across two surfaces with two different hooks; analytics dashboards run BOTH 'report_generation' and 'insights_center' (templates/analytics/dashboard.html:76-78). The primary action 'Generate report' is NOT the verb in code - the governed builder labels its buttons 'Preview' / 'Export CSV' / 'Export JSON' / 'Save', never 'Generate'.

challenges_raised.prior_finding: workflow_click_reduction_audit.json line 49: data_hooks include data-task="parent_payment_receipt", primary_action 'Capture receipt', 'Money Center shows invoice, manual fallback, and receipt capture together.'
challenges_raised.my_finding: FAKE-DONE. grep for data-task="parent_payment_receipt" across the entire tree returns ONLY the audit JSON itself (no template). The actual parent finance template templates/parent/finance.html line 14 uses data-task="parent_payment". Its single-action mode (line 17, gated by rmc_conversion_single_action_enforced) surfaces 'Jump to invoices' as the primary, NOT 'Capture receipt'. The Money Center dashboard (templates/finance/dashboard.html) uses data-task="money_center" with primaries 'Generate fee invoices' / 'Overdue' / 'Payments' / 'Trial balance' / 'Payment Readiness Center' (lines 66-70) - no 'Capture receipt' action exists anywhere visible. This is the clearest fake-done in the click-reduction audit.
challenges_raised.evidence_path: grep data-task="parent_payment_receipt" returns 0 hits in templates/; templates/parent/finance.html:14-17; templates/finance/dashboard.html:66-70

challenges_raised.prior_finding: workflow_click_reduction_audit.json line 63: measurement_status: 'measured_local_route' (the only non-hypothesis claim)
challenges_raised.my_finding: DEFENDED. templates/platform_runtime/manager_offline_sync_center.html lines 15-39 actually exist and contain the explanatory empty-state ('This manager route is intentionally explanatory. It prevents a dead 404 while preserving tenant isolation.') and data-action="offline-sync-select-tenant" at line 36. This claim survives the second pass. However: the audit understates the click count - tenant offline sync also requires school selection within the tenant, so net clicks operator->tenant queue is 2-3, not '1 explanatory action'. The framing 'before/after: 404 to 1 explanatory action' is technically correct but the workflow itself is not closed at one click.

challenges_raised.prior_finding: workflow_click_reduction_audit.json line 73: 'Implementation Command Center exposes go-live score and primary next action.'
challenges_raised.my_finding: DEFENDED. templates/platform_runtime/implementation_command_center.html lines 16-45 actually render: (a) go_live_readiness_score / 100 + band (line 20-22), (b) consolidated_blockers list (line 24-31), (c) Primary next action button (line 43-44). data-rmc-implementation-command-center hook present at line 5. This is the strongest workflow in the audit. Real concern: the page is operator-shell (control_plane_base.html, line 1) so tenant admins cannot reach it - which means the 'tenant_onboarding' label is misleading. It is really operator_onboarding_a_tenant.

challenges_raised.prior_finding: Phase 0 inventory summary lists 'apps_with_help_template: 4' out of 50 apps; workflow_click_reduction_audit does not address help.
challenges_raised.my_finding: GRAVE GAP. Only 4 of 50 apps ship a help template (apicenter, feedback, portal, schools per Phase 0 lines 1025,1741,2038,621). None of the 6 workflows listed in click-reduction audit ship a contextual help link. templates/teacher/attendance.html, marks_entry.html, parent/finance.html, finance/dashboard.html, analytics/governed_report_builder.html - grepped for 'help_contextual_drawer' - only portal_base.html includes it. There is no per-workflow help. Phase 0's 'workflow_templates_without_help' list (20 apps) confirms this. The prompt's question 5 ('Is help / how-to available?') gets a NO across the platform.

challenges_raised.prior_finding: Phase 0 lists 18 apps with ai_helpers import. No earlier audit measures whether the AI guidance is workflow-specific.
challenges_raised.my_finding: UNVERIFIED-BUT-LIKELY-GENERIC. ai_helpers imports surface ONLY through apps/portal/views_ai_*.py (views_ai_gateway, views_ai_copilot, views_ai_draft, views_ai_product, views_ai_surfaces). None of templates/teacher/attendance.html, marks_entry.html, parent/finance.html, finance/dashboard.html have any AI-prompt template binding (no data-rmc-ai-*, no ai-helpers include). The AI Copilot rail (per memory v3.56) lives in the operator control-plane shell, not in tenant workflow pages. Prompt's question 6 ('Is AI guidance specific?') is therefore NO for the 6 click-reduction workflows.
challenges_raised.evidence_path: grep ai-helpers + data-rmc-ai across templates/teacher/ and templates/parent/finance.html returns 0 hits

challenges_raised.prior_finding: No earlier phase measured mobile-usability per workflow.
challenges_raised.my_finding: PARTIAL. Templates do use table-mobile-cards (templates/teacher/attendance.html:45), col-md-* responsive grid (parent/finance.html:51-60), and Bootstrap-grid responsiveness is in place. But the 6 click-reduction workflows have NO mobile-first 'sheet' / bottom-sheet primary CTA (the .rmc-bottom-sheet grammar exists per CLAUDE.md but is not wired into any of these workflows per Phase 0). On a phone, marks_entry.html's per-student grid would degrade to a wide horizontal scroll; the v3.57.1 horizontal-overflow burndown (memory) explicitly targeted that risk but no marks-entry-specific mobile remediation is in evidence. Prompt's question 9 is therefore PARTIAL across all 6 workflows.
challenges_raised.evidence_path: templates/teacher/marks_entry.html: no .rmc-bottom-sheet, no mobile-card-first pattern; CLAUDE.md notes .rmc-bottom-sheet as canonical grammar but not adopted here

challenges_raised.prior_finding: workflow_click_reduction_audit.json lists 6 workflows; Phase 0 inventory lists 27 apps with routes. Studio OS (48 routes per Phase 0) is the entire creator workflow surface yet appears in zero earlier-phase audit entries.
challenges_raised.my_finding: OMISSION. apps/studio_os has 48 routes, 15 workflow templates, surfaces operator+tenant+default. challenges_raised.prior_finding: Phase 0 inventory lists migration_cloud as 92 routes, 136 tests, the platform's biggest single non-API workflow surface; click-reduction audit does not mention it.

recommendations_disputed.earlier_recommendation: Add next-action strip on Teacher Workspace that opens attendance for active class.
recommendations_disputed.my_dispute: This is too shallow. Adding a strip-link does not address the lack of an obvious primary action ON the attendance page itself. The fix needs to be both ends: (a) workspace next-action AND (b) make the in-page primary be 'Save attendance for {class} now' as a sticky bottom-sheet on mobile.
recommendations_disputed.my_alternative: Two-part fix: (1) wire components/workflow_next_action.html into teacher_dashboard with task_code='teacher_attendance' bound to the active class; (2) add an .rmc-bottom-sheet primary 'Save attendance' to templates/teacher/attendance.html with sticky mobile placement.

recommendations_disputed.earlier_recommendation: 'Money Center shows invoice, manual fallback, and receipt capture together.'
recommendations_disputed.my_dispute: Recommendation is out-of-scope for parent surface. Money Center is finance-app dashboard for school finance staff (templates/finance/dashboard.html), NOT a parent surface. Parents see templates/parent/finance.html. Mixing the two is a tenancy / role error.
recommendations_disputed.my_alternative: Rename workflow to 'parent_invoice_pay'. Primary action should be 'Pay invoice {id}' on templates/parent/finance.html if PSP is configured, otherwise 'Mark paid (manual)' with receipt upload. Use data-task='parent_invoice_pay' as the canonical hook; retire the inconsistent data-task='parent_payment' / data-task='parent_payment_receipt' fragmentation.

recommendations_disputed.earlier_recommendation: 'Governed report builder exposes one primary generate/export action.'

recommendations_disputed.my_alternative: Choose the verb. Either 'Preview' is primary (governed_report_builder default) OR rename it to 'Generate'. Pick one and align the data-task hook. Retire the duplicate data-task='report_generation' on decision_intelligence_dashboard.html OR use a different task_code there.

recommendations_disputed.earlier_recommendation: 'Manager route explains tenant scope and sends operator to school selector.'
recommendations_disputed.my_dispute: Recommendation does not address the parallel TENANT-side conflict resolution workflow at /portal/offline/sync/conflicts/ - which is the actual fix-the-data workflow. Operator-side is just routing.
recommendations_disputed.my_alternative: Add a second workflow entry 'tenant_offline_conflict_apply' that audits templates/portal/offline_sync_queue.html lines 75-90 (process-queue, retry-failed, resolve-conflicts). Audit the conflict-resolution rubric (auto-merge vs manual-pick).

category_defining_test_per_workflow.honest_reason: Apple Classroom / Google Classroom open the class roster with one tap and the primary action is taking attendance for *today*. RMC's teacher attendance template makes Export CSV the most prominent button at the top. Until the primary verb on the page matches the user's goal, this fails the bar.

The grid + OCR-paste path is competitive with Powerschool. But the data-task name mismatch breaks any analytics-driven productivity claim. Help-drawer absence is also a gap vs Salesforce in-page help.

Tableau / Looker / Snowflake all open a saved report with one click + 'Refresh' as the primary. RMC fragments into governed_report_export (with Preview as primary) vs decision_intelligence (with insight cards). The user has to pick a surface before they pick an action.

Shopify Pay / Stripe Checkout are the bar: one URL, one card form, done. RMC's parent finance page leads with 'Print' + 'Request finance access' + 'Jump to invoices' - none of which is the action the parent came to do (pay).

The empty-state on the operator manager route is genuinely best-in-class; AWS would call this a 'console-empty-state' pattern. But the tenant-side actual conflict-resolve UX is unaudited; can't claim 10x without seeing it.

go-live score + consolidated blockers + adoption signals + primary-next-action is closer to AWS Account Onboarding than to Salesforce Setup. With adoption telemetry + AI-suggested next step (currently not wired), this could be 10x. As-is, it's strong but not yet category-defining.
